q7.answer: Breach runs are not stored as a counter. The 3-in-a-row check reads the last 3 evaluation rows (ticks T-2, T-1, T), and a non-breaching or missing tick breaks the run. Only healthy_streak is stored, on the incident row. It goes up on a healthy evaluation while an incident is open. It resets to 0 on a rate of 1% or more, a breach, or a missing tick.

q8.answer: Each evaluator computes the same tick from the wall clock and runs a transaction that starts with INSERT evaluation (service, rule, tick) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Only the instance whose insert succeeded updates streaks or opens an incident, so a minute is counted once. A partial unique index on (service, rule) where status is open is a second guard, and escalation steps are written only if the incident row was actually created.

q9.answer: Each step has a fixed absolute due_at (opened_at, +5m, +10m) stored in escalation_step. Workers poll every 5 seconds and claim due pending steps with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. The worker locks the incident row. If the incident is acknowledged or resolved it marks the step cancelled. Otherwise it looks up the on-call person, writes a notification row, marks the step done and sends.

q10.answer: The provider calls the ack webhook with the notification id, signed with a shared secret. The handler verifies the signature, finds the incident through the notification row and locks it. If the incident is open and not yet acknowledged, it sets acked_by and acked_at, cancels all pending escalation steps in one update, and logs an applied ack_log row. Later or duplicate acks are logged as ignored.

q11.answer: It is worked out when the step is claimed and paged, not when the incident opens. The worker asks the schedule service who holds the role (primary, secondary or manager) at that moment. So a 09:00 handover mid-incident pages whoever holds the role then. If the schedule is down, the worker uses the oncall_cache entry. The person paged is stored on the notification row.

q12.answer: When the incident resolves, the resolving transaction inserts a resolved notification for each person already paged. It reads them from the page notification rows, and each resolved row copies the level of its page. The send loop then claims those rows. It does not ask the current on-call schedule. If nobody was paged, no notices are created.
